title: Add Up the Tips of a 7-Point Star | AMC 8-Style Level 4

scenes.visual: Seven points on a circle, the star draws itself point to point (A→C→E→G→B→D→F→A). Line 1: the seven tip angles get small arcs one by one. Line 2: a pencil icon traces the star. Line 3: Vantee title card.
lines: Seven pointy tips on a star. What do their angles add up to?
You don't need to measure a single one. A walking pencil can tell us!
Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's add up some star points.

scenes.visual: Question text left; on the right the circle with seven evenly spaced points labeled A through G going counterclockwise, A at the top (bank figure has no labels — add them, 48px). Line 3: draw A→C, C→E, … one chord at a time. Line 4: tip arcs glow. Line 5: chips 180, 360, 540, 720, 900.
lines: Here's the question.
Seven points are evenly spaced on a circle.
A star is drawn by joining each point to the second point after it, going around the circle.
What is the sum, in degrees, of the seven angles at the tips of the star?
Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

scenes.visual: Line 1: from A, a hop arrow skips B and lands on C ('second point after'). Line 2: all seven tip arcs in purple, all the same size; one labeled 'tip'. Line 3: '7 tips: total = ?'.
lines: So what do we know? Each line skips one point. A joins to C, C joins to E, and so on.
The star is perfectly even, so all seven tips are the same size.
We want the total of all seven tip angles.

scenes.visual: Pause card with countdown ring; star figure visible.
lines: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.visual: Mark center O. Line 2: seven radii to the points, cutting seven equal slices; each center angle labeled s. Line 3: row '7s = 360°'. Line 4: zoom on tip at A: the two star lines from A go to C and to F; draw radii OA, OC, OF. Line 5: triangle OAC shaded green, angle AOC labeled '2s' (spans two slices). Keep right-side panel for equation rows.
lines: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: cut the circle into slices from the center.
Seven equal slices fill the whole turn. Call each slice angle s.
Seven copies of s make three hundred sixty degrees.
Now zoom in on the tip at A. Its two lines go to C and to F.
Draw lines from the center to A and to C. The angle at the center covers two slices, so it's two s.

scenes.visual: Line 1: OA and OC get matching ticks ('radius'). Lines 2-3: row '180 − 2s', then halved: '90 − s' on each base angle of triangle OAC. Lines 4-5: triangle OAF shaded (other side), center angle 2s, base angle at A '90 − s'. Line 6: tip at A = (90 − s) + (90 − s) = 180 − 2s. Lines 7-8: '7 × (180 − 2s) = 1260 − 14s'. Line 9: '14s = 2 × 360 = 720'. Line 10: '1260 − 720 = 540'. Line 11: answer badge '540°' with chime at end, choice C highlighted.
lines: Both of those lines are radii, so they're equal. Triangle O A C is isosceles.
Its angles add to one hundred eighty. Subtract two times the letter s, then split the rest in half.
So each base angle is ninety minus s.
The other side works the same way. Triangle O A F has a two s angle at the center too.
So its angle at A is also ninety minus s.
So the tip at A is ninety minus s, twice. That's one hundred eighty minus two s.
Seven tips make seven times one hundred eighty, minus fourteen times s.
That's one thousand two hundred sixty, minus fourteen s.
Fourteen times s is two times seven times s.
That's two times three hundred sixty, which is seven hundred twenty.
One thousand two hundred sixty minus seven hundred twenty is five hundred forty.
The tips add up to five hundred forty degrees. That's Choice C!

scenes.visual: Pencil arrow at A pointing toward C. Line 2: pencil walks A→C, at C it turns (show the turn angle as an outside arc, green) and heads to E. Line 3: at a tip, label the tip angle (purple) and the turn (green); 'turn + tip = 180'. Line 4: pencil walks the full star; a lap counter around the center ticks 'lap 1' then 'lap 2' (14 slices = 2 laps). Line 5: 'total turn = 2 × 360 = 720'.
lines: Here's a really clever way. Put a pencil at A, pointing at C, and walk it around the star.
At each tip, the pencil turns to head down the next line.
The turn and the tip angle sit on a straight line, so together they make one hundred eighty.
Each line jumps two slices. Seven lines make fourteen slices: two full circles.
Watch the pencil go all the way round. It circles the center twice before it gets home!
Two full circles means two times three hundred sixty degrees of turning. That's seven hundred twenty.

scenes.visual: Lines 1-2: '7 × 180 = 1260' (tips + turns). Lines 3-4: 'tips = 1260 − 720 = 540'. Line 5: small card 'Pencil walk: count the laps'.
lines: At each of the seven tips, the tip plus the turn is one hundred eighty.
Seven times one hundred eighty is one thousand two hundred sixty.
The turns use up seven hundred twenty. So the tips get the rest.
One thousand two hundred sixty minus seven hundred twenty is five hundred forty again!
When would you pick this way? For any star, just count how many times the pencil circles the center.

scenes.visual: Choice chips; wrong ones turn red with a mini-note. Line 2: small five-point star with '180°'. Line 3: plain seven-sided shape (heptagon) with '900°'. Line 4: '720 = the turns'. Line for B: '360 = one full turn' with a small plain-polygon turn circle.
lines: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
Choice A, one hundred eighty, is the famous answer for a five-point star. Seven points is a different star!
Choice E, nine hundred, is the angle total for an ordinary seven-sided shape.
The pencil would circle only once.
Choice D, seven hundred twenty, is the total turning of the pencil, not the tips.
Choice B, three hundred sixty, is one full turn.
That's what the turns of an ordinary shape add to, not a star's tips.
So here's a great habit. Don't use a rule you remember for a different shape. Check it.

scenes.visual: Same seven points; new star joining each point to the THIRD point after it: A→D→G→C→F→B→E→A draws itself. Tips visibly sharper.
lines: Ready for a challenge? Same seven points, but now join each point to the third point after it.
The star gets pointier. What do its seven tip angles add up to?

scenes.visual: Pause card, countdown, the pointier star visible.
lines: Pause the video, and go for it!

scenes.visual: Pencil walks the pointier star; lap counter shows 'lap 1, lap 2, lap 3' over lines 1-2. Rows: '3 × 360 = 1080', '7 × 180 = 1260', '1260 − 1080 = 180'. Answer badge '180°' with chime at end of the 'one hundred eighty degrees!' line. Last line before recap: no new maths.
lines: Let's walk the pencil. Each line now jumps three slices, and seven lines make twenty-one slices.
Twenty-one slices is three full circles.
So the pencil turns three times three hundred sixty, which is one thousand eighty degrees.
Tips plus turns is still seven times one hundred eighty, one thousand two hundred sixty.
One thousand two hundred sixty minus one thousand eighty is one hundred eighty degrees!
Here's the sneaky part. Pointier tips, so a smaller total. If you got one hundred eighty, amazing work!

scenes.visual: Summary card: pencil-walk diagram with 'tip + turn = 180' and 'turns = laps × 360'.
lines: Here's the big idea to remember.
At every corner, the tip and the pencil's turn add to one hundred eighty.
Count how many times the pencil circles the center. Times three hundred sixty is the total turning, and the tips get the rest.
I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
